1.pericope_label: Found of those who did not seek
debates: Whether the first verse speaks of the Gentiles or of Israel
Whether these words answer the prayer of the previous chapter
How the opening verb should be rendered
outliers: Ellicott reads both verses of Israel where Gill, Wesley and Henry follow the apostolic application to the Gentiles
themes: Grace that precedes seeking
An apostolic quotation weighed against the Hebrew
Hands spread out all the day
A reproach turned back on the reader

3.pericope_label: Provocation to his face, and a holiness that is apostasy
debates: Whether the bricks are altars or the flat roofs of houses
Whether frequenting graves is mere uncleanness or necromancy
Whether these practices point to Judah before the exile or to Babylon
outliers: Ellicott argues from the absence of swine in the cuneiform record against a Babylonian setting
themes: Sin committed openly
Sleeping in strange places for an oracle
Separation claimed on the ground of apostasy
A punishment already burning

6.pericope_label: Written before me, and measured first into their bosom
debates: Whether children are punished for their fathers sins or for their own imitation of them
How the clause about recompense should be construed
outliers: Keil and Delitzsch read the word first as preparing the turn to promise, where the others take the verse as pure threatening
themes: A register that forgets nothing
Long-suffering mistaken for forgetfulness
Guilt accumulated across generations
Judgment as the primary duty of a ruler

8.pericope_label: The cluster spared, and the land from Sharon to Achor
debates: Whether the seed out of Jacob is Christ, the apostles, or the returning remnant
Whether the phrase is my mountain or my mountains
Whether the transition from threat to promise is abrupt or prepared
outliers: Clarke reads a singular servant referring to the Messiah where the others read the servants collectively
themes: A remnant according to the election of grace
The righteous few as a reason for sparing many
A vintage song turned to prophecy
Peace measured from coast to wilderness

11.pericope_label: A table set for Gad, and a people numbered to the sword
debates: Whether Gad and Meni are proper names of deities or common nouns
Whether the idolatry described is Canaanite or Babylonian
What the two names denote if they are deities
outliers: Clarke declines the identification that Ellicott and Keil and Delitzsch pursue, holding the loss of that knowledge a mercy
themes: Idolatry named as forgetting the holy mountain
A wordplay that turns Number into a sentence
Judgment neither random nor resistible
Cost spared for idols and grudged to God

13.pericope_label: Servants fed and adversaries hungry, and a new name
debates: Whether the penalties are chosen to answer the particular sin
What it means for a name to be left as a curse
What the title God of the Amen implies
outliers: Ellicott grounds the new name in the faithfulness of God rather than in the disgrace of the old one alone
themes: Punishment shaped to the offence
A parable of the prudent and the foolish servants
A name that becomes a byword
Truth kept as the ground of blessing

17.pericope_label: New heavens, a new earth, and a city created a rejoicing
debates: Whether the new creation is physical, ecclesiastical, or eschatological
Whether the promise belongs to the earthly city or the city above
Whether the silencing of weeping is fulfilled in this life or the next
outliers: Clarke surveys four readings of the new creation and settles on none of the literal ones
themes: A promise that rises above the one before it
Former joys swallowed up as well as former griefs
God rejoicing in the joy he gives
Weeping silenced because death is

20.pericope_label: Days like the days of a tree
debates: Whether the promise is deathless life or restored longevity
Whether sin still exists in the restored city
What span the days of a tree are meant to convey
outliers: Ellicott insists the promise is of individual and not national life
themes: Long life rather than no death
A curse of the law reversed
Enjoying what one has built
Sin present under altered conditions

23.pericope_label: Prayer answered before it is spoken, and the wolf fed with the lamb
debates: Where the phrase my chosen belongs in the verse division
Whether the peace among animals is literal or figurative
Whether the repetition of an earlier passage argues for one author
outliers: Gill and Wesley read the beasts as men where Ellicott takes the discords of nature literally
themes: Labour that is not lost
Prayer anticipated by its answer
Paradise restored
A promise bounded to men
